purpose: Smoke the sparse-pilot theorem with every parameter unknown; compare finite-time behavior to a separately labelled known-parameter oracle, not certify rates from a fitted slope.
seed_rule: base_seed + N; NumPy PCG64, replicates vectorized with independent common pilot per replicate
calibration_schedule: epoch k>=2 begins at 2^k; first floor(2^(k/2))+1 controls c+v; use m lag-two samples; hold old estimates until complete
estimator: exact algorithm in proof.md section 2, scalar projections by clipping
metrics: full-time mean error and original cost
exploitation-only tail metrics explicitly labelled conditional diagnostic
all three parameter errors per epoch
oracle normalized N times mean error and N times predictable cost gap
diagnostic_tail: second half of final epoch, excludes no selected bad observations; all times in this preselected window are exploitation
checks: actual state max <= proven deterministic bound
calibration sample counts and update times
moment map inversion algebra on deterministic matrix example
nonclaims: no finite-sample slope is a proof
scalar smoke does not test all matrix dimensions
